oneLine: The seam to the external retail network: answers its purchase orders in time, tells it what the building can ship, and reports what the dock received.

rows.title: Take a purchase order and hold the stock
rows.story: A new purchase order is recorded and its products are translated to our SKUs. order-management holds the stock and promises a ship date. If the date is feasible, the whole order is accepted.
rows.policy: Whenever a poll finds a new purchase order, record it and start its answer clock

then.does: is told the whole order is accepted; it is settled later

rows.title: Refuse an order we cannot take
rows.story: One unknown product, or a ship-by date the building cannot meet, refuses the whole order. Any stock already held is freed and the network is told no, with the reason.
rows.policy: Whenever a purchase order has an unknown product or an infeasible date, refuse all of it

then.does: is told no, with the reason (unknown listing or cannot meet ship-by)

rows.title: Settle an accepted order
rows.story: The network confirms or refuses an answer later. On success the order is acknowledged and the held stock is released. On failure the hold is freed and the order is refused.
rows.policy: Every pass, ask the network about each accepted order: success settles it, failure refuses it, pending waits

rows.title: Confirm that an order shipped
rows.story: Once acknowledged, an order can be confirmed as shipped. It is normally triggered when outbound-shipping reports the load as shipped; an operator can also do it by hand. The network gets a label request first.

then.does: is sent the label request and then the shipment confirmation

rows.title: Report an order past its answer deadline
rows.story: A sweep finds orders still unanswered after their deadline and reports each one on every pass. It never changes the order itself.
rows.policy: Every sweep, report each unanswered order that is past its deadline, and leave the order unchanged

then.does: opens an exception for the order, or adds to the one already open

rows.title: Refuse an order nobody answered in time
rows.story: A separate sweep refuses orders whose deadline passed unanswered, and frees the held stock if there is a hold. An overdue order is never answered late.
rows.policy: Every sweep, refuse each unanswered order that is past its deadline and free its held stock

rows.title: Free a hold nobody decided
rows.story: order-management never times out a held order, so this context does. An open hold well past the deadline is cancelled and reported. The order's own state is left alone.
rows.policy: Every sweep, cancel any open hold that is past its deadline plus a grace period

then.does: opens an exception for the order, or adds to the one already open

rows.title: Keep the cutoff schedule copy
rows.story: process-path-management announces process paths and their cutoff schedules. A local copy of the cutoffs and path cycle times lets offers and the site profile be worked out without a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever a path or its cutoff schedule changes, update the local copy

rows.title: Keep the path capacity copy
rows.story: wes-work-planning announces how much capacity is left on each path before each cutoff. A local copy lets offers and cutoff ceilings be worked out without a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever a path's remaining capacity changes, update the local copy

rows.title: Work out what we could offer
rows.story: For each known SKU the offer is the lower of the stock usable now and what the paths can still handle before the next feasible cutoff. Unknown capacity falls back to stock.
rows.policy: Every pass, work out an offer per SKU from usable stock and the capacity before the next cutoff

rows.title: Tell the network how the building works
rows.story: In live mode, each site's cutoffs, handling time and order ceilings are derived from the local copies and declared to the network. A new revision is sent only when the content changed.
rows.policy: Every pass, declare each site's operating profile to the network, but only if it changed

then.does: learns each site's cutoffs, handling time and order ceilings

rows.title: Tell the network what we can ship
rows.story: In live mode, the saved offers become an inventory feed per site. The feed is sent when it changed, and repeated at most hourly when it did not.
rows.policy: Every pass, send each site's offers for the items the site lists, when they changed

then.does: learns how many of each listed item the site can ship

rows.title: Announce a seller shipment to receiving
rows.story: In live mode, shipments the network says are on their way are recorded. Each one is registered in inbound-receiving as an expected delivery before the truck arrives. Failures are retried with a growing wait.
rows.policy: Whenever a poll finds a shipped seller shipment, record it and register an expected delivery

rows.title: Keep a copy of the receipts at the dock
rows.story: inbound-receiving announces each accepted carton, each carton finding and each closed receipt. A local copy keeps only the deliveries this context announced, so the result can be reported later.
rows.policy: Whenever a receipt closes, keep it with its cartons and findings, but only for our own deliveries

rows.title: Report what the dock received
rows.story: Each closed receipt is turned into a per-carton result: received, damaged, missing or unexpected, with any findings. It is sent to the network exactly once per shipment.
rows.policy: Every pass, report each closed receipt not yet reported, retrying with a growing wait

then.does: is told what arrived, carton by carton, with the findings

hotspots.text: The deadline warning fires only after the answer deadline has passed. The decision record says it should fire as the deadline approaches.
If releasing the held stock fails after an order settles, nothing retries it: the order no longer counts as awaiting settlement.
The network is always told one package per order, because the shipped-load fact carries no per-order package count yet.
Remaining capacity is counted as one order per unit, so a declared cutoff ceiling can be too high until the network corrects it.
Dock findings with no carton label (unknown product, unlabelled carton) cannot be reported to the network. They are only logged.

opportunities.text: outbound-shipping could add a per-order package count to its shipped-load fact. The consumer already tolerates it, so the real count would flow.
Pack levels from the network's listings could be declared to product-master once the open question of which side owns a product code is settled.
